body:
November, 2016: a tough time to be a human being in the United States. Something had went horribly, horribly wrong, and Trump had taken the election. I watched it on TV with thousands of others from the Democratic party's election night gala in the ballroom of some fancy hotel downtown. I hadn't bothered to vote that day, and that was not the only dark and shameful secret that I harbored: secretly, I had wished for this. Not once would I speak the unspeakable aloud, not before the election, and not for the four years that followed. Aloud I was anti-Trumpism 110%. But privately, I harbored my truth, that I had indeed wished for the catastrophe to strike down on everyone. I was in awe of the power of the vitriolic hatred that he inspired on all sides. It could not be Trump's alone, it was a hatred which belonged to us all. It was who we were. It was what we deserved.
A couple of days earlier, Halloween weekend, I had done something wild and crazy for the purpose of self-amusement. I took an overdose of jimsonweed (crushed, dried leaves, brewed as tea) and went to a nightclub to pass out.
I took an overdose of jimsonweed (crushed, dried leaves, brewed as tea) and went to a nightclub to pass out.
My head was cleanly shaved so that everyone could see the hideous scar which covered my entire scalp: scary, right? I donned a cheap, sparkly black face mask over my eyes, and went to "the Place," in Uptown. This was an interracial nightclub: insofar as, probably every race was represented there except white guys, who, apparently, preferred to dance anywhere BUT the Place. So then I, with my shaved head and glaring deformity, was the exception to the rule. I had drunk the jimsonweed tea minutes before entering, on Friday, the 28th of October. I told myself: I did not plan for this to be one of those blackout nights. But I think, deep down, it gave me a perverse thrill.
I ordered a flute of Prosecco and managed a few sips. I was super tired. Hours were lost. I was walking around outside, trying to walk in the direction of home, not sure exactly which direction to take to get there. Finally, I saw my house, and walked up the steps. But something was wrong. The electronic keypad, that unlocked the front door, had disappeared. Frantically I turned the doorknob. It was locked. A horrible sinking feeling set in, as I grasped what had happened: they had changed the locks on me! They had changed the locks in my own home, to keep me out! I stared helplessly. Then I did a double take. Oh, fuck! I was standing on someone else's porch! I collected myself and hurried away. I had certainly been close, at least: my door was just two or three houses down. I went inside and took stock of everything. My wallet was gone. My cheap mask, gone too. A small hole torn in the front of my shirt indicated to me that there had been an aggressive confrontation, the details of which, I knew nothing. I couldn't stand it.
This had to be the fifth or sixth latenight blackout sustained in two years.
